analysis.summary: Patch first what is already being exploited: Google says a PRC-nexus actor used the vCenter authentication bypass CVE-2026-123890 as a zero-day, an investigating firm reports Cisco Expressway clusters breached after public exploit code (Cisco has not confirmed), and Confluence, N-central, Apache Roller and four flaws CISA listed on Nov 18 are under attack. NGINX2Root remains the broadest exposure, now showing up in appliances such as Synology DSM. Supplier breaches keep reaching customers: the PLAID KARTE and Fireworks AI cascades are joined by JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard provider incidents and Boone County's clinic operator. The European Commission confirmed an AI-assisted attack, and Bulgaria and the USDA disclosed government intrusions. Healthcare filed the most breach notices, mostly for intrusions months old. The outage wave remains a cluster in time only.

patterns.title: NGINX2Root: HTTP/2 code execution, public exploit code, and appliances that bundle NGINX
patterns.narrative: F5 shipped fixes for five NGINX flaws. Two in HTTP/2 handling, CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633, let an unauthenticated attacker run code as the nginx worker; Wiz says CVE-2026-123007 affects every version since 1.9.5, and fixes are in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9. CERT-FR knows of a public proof of concept and SecurityWeek says Rapid7 and Censys published one. Xint, which found the flaws, chained one with a separate, still-unpatched Linux kernel SCTP bug to reach root, including out of a Docker container. NGINX fronts a large share of web services and sits inside ingress controllers and appliances, so this is the week's broadest exposure. On Nov 19 Synology listed the same CVE-2026-123007 among fixes for its DSM storage operating system, the first appliance vendor on file to do so, and CERT-SE issued its own warning. Disabling HTTP/2 is CERT-FR's interim workaround.
patterns.caveat: No exploitation in the wild is reported by F5, CERT-FR, Wiz or SecurityWeek. Sources differ on whose proof of concept is public (Wiz withholds its own), and F5's own advisory could not be read. The kernel flaw has no CVE and Xint withholds its details. The Apache mod_http2 flaw that Singapore says is exploited is in different software and is grouped here only because the protocol is the same. Synology's advisory does not say whether its NGINX build is reachable over HTTP/2 by default.

edges.rel: same flaws, proof of concept published
chained to kernel bug for root (Xint)
same CVE-2026-123007, fixed in Synology DSM

patterns.title: Exploited now: vCenter, Expressway, Confluence, N-central and other edge systems
patterns.narrative: Exploitation is reported for a run of internet-facing and management systems this week. Google says the PRC-nexus actor ARMORY CASTLE exploited the VMware vCenter authentication bypass CVE-2026-123890 as a zero-day, with Rapid7 dating activity to September. The firm F6 investigated an intrusion through Cisco Expressway clusters after proof-of-concept code was posted for CVE-2026-76466. CISA listed the Apache Axis flaw behind Confluence takeovers, plus Synology DSM, LiteLLM and REDCap flaws, as exploited; N-central servers were hit through zero-days; Apache says the Roller flaw is exploited; Singapore warns of Apache mod_http2 exploitation; CISA added Puppet Enterprise and Check Point Gaia; Huntress tracks rogue ScreenConnect clients pushed to hundreds of hosts; and Dorsata was breached through a Metabase zero-day. Dragos says industrial ransomware this quarter mostly entered through edge devices, which matches this list. These are the patches to apply before the merely critical ones.
patterns.caveat: Each exploitation claim is about one product and is stated by an agency, vendor or investigating firm, but they are different attackers; grouping them is by attribute. Cisco's advisory still says Cisco knows of no malicious use of the Expressway flaw, so that case rests on F6 as reported by SecurityWeek. Rapid7 says the Confluence and N-central exploitation was reported together, not that one actor did both. The Dorsata intrusion happened in August.

patterns.title: Critical fixes with public exploit code but no attacks reported yet
patterns.narrative: A second tier of flaws has fixes and, in several cases, public exploit code, but no reported attacks. CISA told organisations to patch the Java4Shell flaw CVE-2026-114938 immediately, and Oracle's November update carries the fix. Depthfirst published phpAfterShell, which reaches code execution on PHP's default session handler despite October's PHP2Shell fixes, the same day PHP shipped releases fixing 17 flaws. Depthfirst also published database exploits for PostgreSQL, MySQL, ClickHouse and Oracle. NCSC Netherlands knows of public exploit code for Ivanti Endpoint Manager; Drupal, WordPress, F5 BIG-IP and Synology DSM shipped critical fixes; SonicWall says Gen 6 firewalls will get no more patches. Australia's ACSC warns that the gap between disclosure and exploitation keeps shrinking, which is why public code matters more than a score.
patterns.caveat: No exploitation is reported for any of these at the time of writing; that public code will soon be used is our inference, drawn from the pattern in the exploited list, not a finding. The research exploits have not been independently reproduced, and the sources do not say which PHP release fixes phpAfterShell.

edges.rel: same day, likely same PHP releases

patterns.title: Breached suppliers with named customers: PLAID KARTE and Fireworks AI
patterns.narrative: Two supplier breaches now have customers that say they were hit through them. PLAID suspended its KARTE customer-data service after unauthorized access on Nov 13, with account emails and integration credentials listed as leaked. On Nov 18 BASE FOOD said about 710,000 customer names and emails linked to KARTE leaked, and DHC said about 19.11 million online-shop customer records leaked after the KARTE access. Fireworks AI confirmed two intrusions on Nov 17, the second exposing account and billing data for every account made before Oct 30; Cursor says a key it issued to Fireworks led to trojanized Claude Code extension builds, Notion says some AI chat transcripts were accessed, and Uber's breach of about 150,000 people is reported as involving Fireworks. Each supplier held data or keys for many customers, so more notices are likely.
patterns.caveat: PLAID's own notice was read only through a secondary summary, and DHC's figures come from NHK, Kyodo and Yomiuri. Sources do not always say which Fireworks incident reached which customer, and the Uber link rests on a spokesperson statement reported second-hand. Other KARTE or Fireworks customers have not been named, so counts will change.

patterns.title: Breaches through a provider, not the front door
patterns.narrative: Beyond the two named cascades, many confirmed breaches this week came through a supplier. Swiss federal pension fund Publica must assume member data leaked from a test environment after an attack on its software supplier PK Softech; about 40 Irish credit unions were exposed through Wellington IT; DHL employee data was copied from a survey provider; Office Partner's customer data was reached at an external service provider. JPMorganChase says vendors that serve it were attacked and marketing data with some customer names and emails was accessed, while Mastercard and Visa reported provider incidents the same day. Boone County, Indiana, says its employees' health data was exposed through Marathon Health, which runs its clinic. Optimizely's injected script reached 178 organisations' sites, and N-able disclosed access to a Mail Assure and SpamExperts server. Infoblox, La Poste's Maileva and Osaka's email delivery service add to the list.
patterns.caveat: These are separate vendors and separate attackers; the shared element is the route, not the actor, and grouping them is our inference. JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard have not named their providers or said whether it is the same one; the n0n gang's claim is unverified. N-able says it has no evidence customer mail was compromised.

edges.rel: same day, providers not named, link unknown

patterns.title: AI-driven attack tooling (ARTEX, Cairn)
patterns.narrative: The FBI, Cisco Talos, Amazon and Cloudflare each describe intrusions or scanning run with the open-source ARTEX agent platform; Cloudflare says AI pentest traffic rose about 30-fold since October. Google reports a PRC-nexus group building its own automated attack tool and an exploit_agent framework that turned patches into working exploits. The European Commission's spokesman confirmed on Nov 19 that the attack first detected on Oct 22, which took down its Sysper HR system and the JSIS health insurance scheme, was carried out with a publicly available AI tool; the Commission found no staff-wide data breach and named no attacker.
patterns.caveat: Same tools, different actors. ARTEX is open source, so a shared tool is a shared attribute, not a link between intrusions, and says nothing about who is behind them. The FBI and Talos both cite more than 2,250 downstream tenants but describe the case differently; that they are one case is our inference. The Commission did not name the tool, so it may not be any of those listed here.

patterns.title: Developer and AI-agent toolchains as the target
patterns.narrative: Separate incidents aim at the tools developers and AI agents run with. Bitdefender found 22 GitHub links whose AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md files tell coding assistants to run a loader, and Google describes a North Korean cluster planting a backdoor through Claude Code settings files: the agent's own instruction files are now an attack route. A credential stealer sat in Microsoft's Agent Framework package on PyPI, and trojanized Claude Code extension builds reached Cursor's marketplace cache. A study of 428 LLM API routers found some injecting code and misusing credentials, and researchers took over the Kokoro model's Hugging Face account through an expired domain. Microsoft showed in a lab how a phished device-code approval could steer a coding agent. The prize in each is the keys and tokens these tools hold.
patterns.caveat: These are different actors and methods; no source connects them. The Microsoft device-code work, the router study and the Kokoro takeover are research, not attacks seen in the wild; the Kokoro researchers did not upload altered weights.

patterns.title: Reused passwords and phished device codes open accounts
patterns.narrative: Several services saw accounts opened with credentials rather than exploits. Hydro-Québec says an intruder used email and password pairs from elsewhere and asked about 1.7 million customers to reset passwords; Japan's Takarakuji lottery had 4,436 accounts entered in a password list attack; Germany's BundID citizen accounts faced a mass automated login wave and were blocked as a precaution; TfL took its Oyster photocard site offline after account compromises. Separately, Hornetsecurity describes device-code phishing in which victims enter a code on Microsoft's real sign-in page and hand tokens to the attacker, the same technique Microsoft showed against coding agents. Marathon Health, which runs Boone County's employee clinic, says a voice-phishing call gave an attacker access to its systems. Multifactor sign-in and blocking device-code flow where it is not needed answer both.
patterns.caveat: Different attackers and services; no source connects them. TfL has not said how accounts were compromised, and BundID officials see no evidence that data was taken. The Microsoft coding-agent case is a lab demonstration.

patterns.title: Outage wave: close in time, causes self-reported, and real knock-on harm
patterns.narrative: Outages hit well-known US services within a week: Microsoft 365, the FAA ground stop, the National Weather Service, Workday, Chase, United, Marriott, Charles Schwab, Apple and the NSA's classified network, with Japan's Docomo failing on Nov 16. NBC reported on Nov 19 that an NSA outage was still under way and, citing sources, not cyber-caused. The outages are linked only by timing. Where a cause was given it was the organisation's own, most often a planned change: a capacity upgrade at Microsoft, a router fault at the FAA, a software release at Chase, maintenance and, per the DNI, a PHP patch at the NSA. Officials see no cyberattack. The Microsoft outage did cause stated harm: attackers used it as a phishing lure, and a hotel report says it blocked a chlorine alert email before 15 guests were poisoned. Lawmakers are pressing for explanations.
patterns.caveat: Officials say these were not attacks and not coordinated. Workday, Marriott, Schwab and United published no cause, Google disputes a broad Gmail outage, and the FAA trigger is undetermined. That NBC's Nov 19 report describes the same NSA outage as the Nov 17 NSA Net failure is our inference. The hotel report comes from one outlet. The Microsoft outage itself began on Nov 12, just before this window.

edges.rel: a day apart, no stated link
likely the same NSA outage, not stated

patterns.title: Refrigeration controllers under attack, and Iran in the frame
patterns.narrative: Midnight Blue says attack waves on internet-exposed refrigeration controllers started in France on Oct 11, and this week disclosed six unpatched pre-authentication flaws in Danfoss controllers. VulnCheck disclosed 14 flaws in end-of-life Copeland XWEB EVO supervisors and saw two targeted within a day. France says it will seek EU sanctions on an IRGC cyber unit over the French attacks, and Italy's prime minister briefed the opposition on hybrid threats after supermarket and school incidents. In Washington, DHS testimony says Iran-linked actors have stepped up activity against US transport, healthcare, water, energy and financial networks since the US-Iran war began.
patterns.caveat: The attribution to an IRGC unit is the French government's; Iran routinely denies such operations and Midnight Blue says attribution remains open. No source ties the Copeland probing or the US activity to the French campaign; linking the French and US accusations is our inference from the shared accused state. The October attacks themselves are outside the map's window.

edges.rel: controllers hit in French attack waves

patterns.title: Government networks: long-hidden intrusions and state-linked espionage
patterns.narrative: Several governments disclosed intrusions this week. Bulgaria says unidentified hackers sat in state networks from 2021 and took over 62 million pages of documents. Nextgov reports USDA took applications offline for days and reset database passwords in every environment after an internal security incident. The European Commission confirmed an AI-assisted attack that took down HR and health-insurance systems. On the research side, Google says the PRC-nexus ARMORY CASTLE exploited a vCenter zero-day for espionage; Rapid7 attributes a stealthy SoftEther VPN bridge to Webworm, which targets European governments; Bitdefender's EggStreme backdoor still targets Philippine government bodies; Unit 42 and Kaspersky describe espionage over HTTP/3 and through GitHub and SharePoint; Google shows Russia's COLD RELIC using data stolen from one US organisation to phish another. On North Korea, Genians ties a NodeLinkRAT campaign to Kimsuky, Google describes a cluster backdooring crypto developers, and Talos tracks a crypto-stealing group it ties to North Korea with low confidence.
patterns.caveat: Bulgaria, USDA and the Commission have named no attacker, and nothing ties them to each other or to the research reports; USDA's incident rests on anonymous sources and an internal email. Attributions are the vendors' own, at moderate or low confidence for Webworm, Kimsuky and Talos's cluster. The research reports are grouped by type and some describe older activity.

patterns.title: Healthcare: two hospitals disrupted, and breach notices months after the fact
patterns.narrative: Healthcare filed the most breach notices on file this week, and two attacks disrupted care directly. The Greiz-Ronneburg district hospital in Germany closed its emergency room on Nov 15 after an extortion attack, and Monadnock Community Hospital in New Hampshire diverted ambulances after a phone and network outage it now confirms was a cyber incident. Most other notices describe intrusions found months earlier: Access Dental Management (341,049 people, May), Valley Family Health Care and LifeTouch Health (March), MPOWERHealth (June 2025), Hood River Dental (two incidents, 2025 and January 2026), Lansing Urgent Care (September), Dorsata (August, through a Metabase zero-day) and Geisinger (August). Atticus Administration's claims database for New York City retirees and Marathon Health's clinic systems were reached through providers. Social Security numbers and treatment details recur, so these feed fraud and extortion long after the intrusion.
patterns.caveat: These are separate organisations and attackers; the sector is the only shared attribute and grouping them is our inference. Notice dates reflect US reporting rules, so the count says more about disclosure timing than about attack volume. INC Ransom's claim on Lansing Urgent Care is the group's, not the clinic's.

edges.rel: both disrupted emergency care, no stated link

direct: NGINX Open Source and Plus from 1.9.5 with HTTP/2 can be made to run code as the nginx worker without a login; fixes are in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9, and proof-of-concept code is public for one flaw.
downstream: Xint chained one flaw with an unpatched Linux kernel SCTP bug to reach root and escape a Docker container, so a web front end can become a host compromise.

NGINX is embedded in load balancers, Kubernetes ingress controllers and appliances that update on their vendors' schedules; Synology has already listed the same CVE in DSM, so expect more appliance advisories.
watch_for: Ingress and appliance vendors shipping fixed NGINX builds
Worker crashes on HTTP/2 traffic
A Linux kernel fix and CVE for the SCTP flaw
Reports of in-the-wild exploitation
Appliance advisories naming CVE-2026-123007

direct: An unauthenticated attacker can bypass authentication on VMware vCenter Server (CVE-2026-123890, CVSS 9.8); Google says ARMORY CASTLE exploited it as a zero-day, and Rapid7 reports activity from as early as September. Fixes include vCenter 8.0 U3m; there is no workaround.
downstream: vCenter controls every virtual machine it manages, so one compromised server can expose a whole virtual estate.
Exploitation predates the fix, so patching does not show whether a server was already entered; logs back to September matter.
watch_for: vCenter servers reachable from untrusted networks
Unexpected vCenter sign-ins or new local accounts
Hunting guidance and indicators from Google and Broadcom
Victims named in follow-up reporting

direct: PLAID suspended all KARTE services after unauthorized access on Nov 13; account emails and integration credentials are listed as leaked, along with part of the data customers imported.
downstream: DHC says about 19.11 million customer records and BASE FOOD about 710,000 customers' names and emails leaked through KARTE.
Integration credentials held by the service may open customers' own systems, and leaked customer lists feed targeted phishing in Japanese.
watch_for: Further KARTE customers announcing leaks
Phishing that uses shop names and dates of birth
Use of integration keys connected to KARTE

direct: Account and billing data for every Fireworks AI account created before Oct 30 was exposed; some customers' secrets, model files and datasets were reached earlier.
downstream: Cursor, Notion and Uber are reported as affected customers; keys held by the provider led to a trojanized extension at Cursor.
Credentials pasted into AI prompts or held by inference providers can open systems far from the provider itself.
watch_for: Notices from AI and inference providers you use
Use of API keys issued to providers
Secrets in AI chat logs and traces

direct: Any service that decodes untrusted Base64 on an affected x86-64 HotSpot Java runtime could be crashed or taken over without a login.
downstream: Java is bundled inside third-party applications, appliances and container images, so exposure extends to products you did not build.
Patching depends on each vendor shipping an updated runtime, so some systems will stay exposed after your own servers are fixed.
watch_for: Unexpected JVM crashes and restarts
Vendor advisories naming a bundled Java runtime
Signs of exploitation reported by CISA or vendors

direct: Self-hosted Confluence Data Center with the Remote API enabled can be taken over without a login; CISA lists the Axis flaw as exploited.
downstream: In the case Rapid7 saw, the intruder took database credentials, queried a cloud data warehouse and signed in to Microsoft 365 as a service account.
Apache Axis 1.x is end-of-life and may sit inside other Java products that will not get a fix.
watch_for: Unusual Remote API requests to Confluence
Service accounts signing in from new places
Other products bundling Apache Axis 1.x

direct: Internet-facing N-central servers were exploited through zero-days published without coordinated disclosure; crypto miners were deployed.
downstream: An RMM server reaches every managed client, so a compromise can spread to many customer networks at once.
Removal of the Legacy API may break older integrations that still depend on it.
watch_for: N-central servers not on Hotfix 3
New agents or scripts pushed from RMM
Mining processes on managed endpoints

direct: Malicious JavaScript was injected into some Optimizely Web Experimentation customer projects, reaching 178 organisations by one researcher's count.
downstream: Coverage says the code skimmed payment cards and swapped crypto addresses on customers' sites, so their visitors were the victims.
Sites that load third-party scripts without integrity checks or a strict Content-Security-Policy inherit the supplier's compromise.
watch_for: Unexpected scripts on checkout pages
CSP violation reports
Notices from script and tag vendors

direct: Six unpatched pre-authentication flaws let attackers take over Danfoss AK-SM800A refrigeration controllers; hundreds are reachable online.
downstream: Food retail, cold storage and pharmacies risk spoiled stock and safety incidents; French attacks on such controllers were linked to fires.
France is seeking EU sanctions over the campaign, which could prompt further attacks or warnings.
watch_for: Refrigeration controllers reachable from the internet
Unexpected setpoint or alarm changes
CVE numbers and fixes from Danfoss

direct: Equinor's IT systems are under an ongoing attack; it says production is unaffected and email was reported down.
downstream: Restoration time is unknown, so partners and suppliers may see delays or unusual messages from Equinor.
Attackers often use a known incident to send fake invoices or updates in the victim's name.
watch_for: Messages claiming to come from Equinor
Norwegian authority advisories
Any named attacker or leak claim
